fatal_errors: The as-deposited films and nanoribbons are incorrectly assumed to be coarse, ordered hexagonal materials exhibiting a first-order magnetostructural transition; the target material is amorphous or extremely fine/disordered, with only cubic-type short-range order.

The proposed grain-boundary refinement and homogenized nucleation mechanism is inapplicable because no developed crystalline grains or first-order magnetostructural transition were established in the as-deposited state.
Annealing and cyclic strain are combined into one intervention, preventing separation of annealing-induced short-range relaxation from magnetoelastic strain effects.

The predicted reduction of transition hysteresis and smoothing of a sharp entropy peak do not match the observed broad, modest magnetocaloric response or the reported annealing-induced increase in magnetization and peak entropy change.
The hypothesis omits the central geometry-dependent inter-ribbon coupling and magnetic decoupling at 2 micrometre spacing.
explanation: The response recognizes potentially relevant controls—annealing, elastic strain, and nanostructuring—and proposes comparison with an untreated sample. However, it transfers the ordered bulk-alloy first-order-transition picture directly to sputtered films. In the target system, 700 K annealing preserves the amorphous/disordered matrix while causing short-range atomic reordering and residual-strain relaxation, which improves exchange alignment, ferromagnetic volume fraction, magnetization, and the entropy-change peak. Elastic strain up to 2% instead enhances magnetization mainly above 100 K without shifting the approximately 70 K blocking peak, while ribbon spacing controls inter-ribbon coupling. The proposed combined treatment is also poorly discriminating because any change could not be assigned independently to annealing or strain. It lacks the relevant quantitative boundaries—700 K pre-crystallization annealing, 0–2% elastic strain, 40–200 K conventional response with an inverse effect below 20 K, fields up to 50 kOe—and supplies no supporting evidence.
